long_biography.plain_text:
Herbert Wertheim grew up above his father's Florida bakery after his family left Philadelphia. Dyslexia made school difficult, and at sixteen he chose Navy service over reform school. The Navy trained him in aviation electronics and helped him earn a GED; after discharge he worked nights to support college and later won a scholarship to study optometry.

Clinical research led Wertheim to connect ultraviolet exposure with cataracts and retinal damage. He developed protective tints for plastic lenses, briefly sold an earlier laboratory business, then established Brain Power Incorporated to manufacture optical chemicals and instruments. Rather than taking outside investors, he reinvested the company's earnings in technology and industrial stocks over decades. The eye-care enterprise became the capital base for a much larger investment portfolio.
